defects.title: Two-letter element symbols beginning with C are counted as one carbon
defects.trigger: a metabolite whose formula contains Ca, Cl, Co, Cu, Cr, Cd, Ce or Cs, for example metFormulas {'Cl'; 'Ca'; 'CaC2O4'} in a model with one reaction that uses the three metabolites, findCarbonRxns(model, 1)
defects.observed: MATLAB R2025a: nCarbon = [1 1 1]; the regular expression C(\d*) of line 42 matches the C of the element symbol and an empty digit group counts as one carbon at line 50, so chloride and calcium are reported as carbon-containing metabolites and the reaction is in hiCarbonRxns for every threshold up to 1; calcium oxalate counts 1 carbon instead of 2
defects.expected: nCarbon = [0 0 2], the number of carbon atoms in each formula

notes: SEVERITY DECISION for the lead: the limitation entry could be read as wrong-result (a documented input, an elemental formula with Ca or Cl, gives a wrong carbon count); recorded as limitation because the comment at line 41 documents the C(\d*) choice deliberately (to catch one-carbon formulas that do not start with C, e.g. CHO3, which the test pins) and every formula without such a symbol is counted correctly; as wrong-result it would quarantine findCarbonRxns and block its caller multiProductionEnvelope. Probe (R2025a): nCarbon for formulas {'Cl','Ca','CHO3','C6H12O6','H2O','CaC2O4'} = [1 1 1 6 0 1]. The sibling findHiCarbonRxns (regex ^C(\d+)) does not have the behaviour. Pinned: a reaction without any metabolite is listed in zeroCarbonRxns (all of its zero metabolites have no carbon), consistent with the documentation. extra_edges: parseMetNames and columnVector are called for every input (both already tested).

Run-time callees: none in src. Hand-built eight-reaction model reaches every branch (reversible and irreversible format, inclObjFlag on and off, models without c and without lb). E. coli core (probe, R2025a): the structural rule selects exactly the 20 EX_ reactions, 7 of them with lb < 0 (EX_co2, EX_glc, EX_h, EX_h2o, EX_nh4, EX_o2, EX_pi), 21 with inclObjFlag (biomass added); no non-EX_ reaction has a single coefficient. Note on the documentation: NOTE says exchange reactions have one non-zero element of +1 / -1, and the code indeed rejects a single coefficient of -2 (pinned).

One line: printGPRForRxns(model, rxnIDs, 0), called for every input (extra_edges; already tested). test/verifiedTests/analysis/testPrint/testPrintGPRForRxns.m (lines 57-78) also exercises findGPRFromRxns, but it is the test of printGPRForRxns, not a differently named legacy test of this function alone, so a dedicated file was written (III-Naming). The test cannot assert that nothing is printed without evalc (VII-A), so it only checks the returned rules. Probe (R2025a): the error for an unknown abbreviation given as a cell is "The following reaction IDs are not part of this model:\nnotARxn\n" (no identifier); the char form of an unknown name was not probed (the legacy test only asserts that it errors).

Run-time callees: none in src. Branches: cell list (ismember), char found, char not found (0), gene listed twice in model.genes (first position, line 28). Fixture: four-reaction createModel model whose genes g1, g2, g3 come from the gene-reaction rules in order of first appearance (asserted).

Callee defects (in findSubSystemsFromGenes, not in findSubSysGen; that function is not quarantined in this feature, its two defects were recorded by feature 20261104 in its test header): (a) line 87 unique([allSubs{:}]) turns char subSystems into letters, but only in the first output, which findSubSysGen discards, so findSubSysGen is correct for char and for cell subSystems (both pinned; probe on E. coli core: 137 x 2, b0008 -> 'Pentose Phosphate Pathway'); (b) a model with grRules but neither rxnGeneMat nor rules stops at line 76 (regexptranslate) - reached through findSubSysGen, input not used. defects.title: The documented output is not assigned with the default printLevel, so a call requesting it stops
defects.trigger: coupledRxnReport = printCouplingConstraints(model), or with printLevel 0, on a model with a field C, for example the three-reaction model (rxns R1, R2, R3; S = [-1 1 0; 0 -1 1]) with C = [1 -2 0; -1 0 1], d = [0; 1], dsense = ['G'; 'L'] and ctrs = {'c1'; 'c2'}
defects.observed: MATLAB R2025a: Output argument "coupledRxnReport" (and possibly others) not assigned a value in the execution with "printCouplingConstraints" function. The report is only built inside if printLevel > 0 (line 34) and the else branch of line 87 only covers a model without C. Without an output the same call returns silently; with printLevel 1 the same model gives the two-row table (c1 'R1 - R2 >= 0', c2 '- R1 + R3 <= 1'), with printLevel 2 the six-row table with the reaction formulas, and a model without C gives [] for every printLevel

notes: Severity follows the precedent of waves 09, 10 and 12 (documented output not assigned -> error, quarantine). REACH for the lead: the defect is confined to one call form - the output is requested and printLevel <= 0 on a model with field C; calls without an output, or with printLevel >= 1, work (probe: printLevel 1 gives the 2 x 2 table, printLevel 2 the 6 x 4 table with rxnId and formula, a model without C gives 0 x 0 double). The only src caller, XomicsToModel line 1414 disp(printCouplingConstraints(model, param.printLevel)), requests the output and therefore reaches the defect whenever param.printLevel is 0 (XomicsToModel is already BLOCKED by getCobraSolverParams).
